top_story_title: Fortinet ships critical fixes for FortiOS and FortiManager and withholds the details until November 10
top_story_summary: Fortinet released security hardening updates last week for FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator, but is not publishing the vulnerability details until November 10, 2026. In an advance announcement, Fortinet CISO Carl Windsor said the flaws were uncovered with the help of AI models and validated by humans, and warned that attackers have the same AI tooling available to find vulnerabilities and build exploits.
top_actions: Inventory FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator instances with their running builds, and treat anything with an internet-facing management or VPN interface as first in the queue.
Upgrade FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer before the devices they manage - the management platform is the higher-value target and should not be left behind the fleet.
Move FortiGate upgrades into the next change window, HA pair secondary first, and verify config sync and session failover before promoting.

Remove HTTPS/SSH/API administrative access from untrusted and internet-facing interfaces now; restrict the management plane to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network while the upgrades roll out.
Enforce phishing-resistant MFA on all administrative and SSL VPN accounts and remove shared local admin accounts.
executive_summary: Fortinet has shipped fixes for FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator but is withholding the vulnerability details until November 10, 2026 - upgrade on the builds, not on the advisory.
Fortinet says the flaws were found with AI assistance and validated by humans, and warns that attackers have the same tooling; the public-build/private-advisory gap is the exposure window.

Palo Alto Networks PSIRT has rated the impact of two critical PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on its products as HIGH; the collected entry names no products, versions or fixed releases.
Unpatched Tailscale SSH flaws let an attacker who already controls one node reach root on other servers when ACLs permit port forwarding - a lateral-movement problem for overlay remote access.

Unit 42 has retracted its assessment that PHP2Shell flaws were exploited against a European government agency, while scanning and exploitation attempts linked to suspected North Korean activity continue.
key_actions: **Fortinet** — Inventory every FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator instance with its running build, and rank internet-facing management and VPN interfaces first.

**Fortinet** — Upgrade FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer ahead of the devices they manage; take the current builds and fixed-release confirmation from the vendor's own release notes rather than any third-party version claim.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Open the PSIRT advisory for CVE-2026-109618 and confirm which Palo Alto Networks products and versions it lists against your inventory before planning any change.

**Palo Alto Networks** — Apply the fixed release named in the advisory, or the documented workaround if a maintenance window is not available yet; do not act on a version number that the advisory does not state.

ai_defenses.solution: AI-assisted vulnerability discovery in Fortinet product security, human-validated (no product name given in the source)
ai_defenses.what_it_does: Fortinet states that the vulnerabilities fixed in its recent FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator updates were uncovered with the help of AI models and then validated by humans. Its CISO describes this as a response to attackers having the same AI tooling for finding vulnerabilities and building exploits.

headlines.title: Unpatched Tailscale SSH Flaws Could Let a Hacked Device Reach Root on Other Servers
headlines.summary: Unpatched Tailscale SSH flaws let an attacker who already controls one node reach root on other servers it is permitted to connect to, when port forwarding is allowed.

headlines.title: PHP2Shell Exploitation Attempts Continue Amid Suspected N. Korea Global Scanning Activity
